items.text: Confirmed provider's schedule template (visit lengths, slot types, double-book rules, admin/charting blocks) at 3-month pre-start conversation.
Planned DAX Copilot setup ~2 weeks before start; Day-1 instruction by MD.
Captured provider's Epic ID (5-digit; Epic menu > Session Information Report); gave to provider for keyboard fallback if swipe/print fails.

items.section: First Week Email to New Hire and Office Manager
items.text: Sent first-week site-info email to new hire + OM covering emergency protocols (codes, AED, evac, who calls 911), POC testing workflows (strep/flu/COVID/UA/glucose/Hgb), and procedure inventory (joint inj / skin biopsy / I&D / cryo — supplies, billing, consent).
Physical site tour (exam rooms, lab, supply, sample closet, vaccine fridge, AED) by office staff or OM.
Established communication channels: OM, MD, and Marc (Senior Regional MD).
Set up Epic Out-of-Office and in-basket coverage assignments for PTO.
Reviewed call schedule, after-hours triage line, urgent-issue patient instructions.

items.section: Daily Workflow Foundations (Day 1 or 2 with Medical Director)
items.text: Walked through daily huddle (timing, attendees, content); tied to closing care gaps as the reason it matters.

items.section: Daily Workflow Foundations (Day 1 or 2 with Medical Director)
items.text: Walked through care-gap identification on the daily schedule and how to close them in the visit.
Walked through message-pool management including lab results.
Set up ≥5 Quick Action buttons covering most incoming results. Reinforce: these aren't typed individually — that's what makes them fast.
Created additional Quick Actions / SmartPhrases for routine guidance: BG control, BP control, cholesterol, exercise, repeat-lab timing.
Taught response patterns for every in-basket category: staff messages, cosign orders, patient requests, MyChart, HCC dept, internal pharmacist, billing.
Rearranged LOS and E/M buttons for the new provider (very beginning — first session).
Walked through level 3/4/5 billing; stressed accurate level selection.
Reviewed E/M Pro use.
Showed where HCC codes appear in Epic and on the daily schedule.
Moved the HCC column all the way to the left of the schedule view.
Reviewed This Visit tab HCC management: agree / stable / disagree / managed-by-other-provider. Majority should be 'agree' — curated by team research.
Covered CAHPS and HOS basics; tied to performance.
Showed vitals entry; confirmed repeated when clinically indicated.
Showed CC entry; stressed CC required for telemed billable.
Showed allergy entry.
Showed PMH/PSH/SH/FH entry; reinforced SH alongside the rest.
Walked through cleaning/reconciling med list + dx list thoroughly; doing it makes future visits easier.
Walked through writing/closing progress notes using SmartPhrases built into top-of-note buttons.
Discussed creating new SmartPhrases from already-written/transcribed statements.
Established + provided a standard progress note that pulls vitals from last 3 visits (not just most recent).
Showed how to run a telehealth visit end-to-end.
EKG ordering, performance, interpretation workflow.
Showed AWV SmartSet location, selection, AWV progress note.
Clinical staff member walked new provider through AWV questionnaire so provider can complete one solo if needed.
Reinforced running AWV themselves is not required, just useful.
Below AWV note heading, all current specialists must be listed.
Labs ordered in AWV (or otherwise) must attach to a diagnosis, not a screening code, so Medicare covers and patient isn't billed.
Covered SDOH screening within reason as it ties into AWV SmartSet/questionnaire.
BH screening: PHQ-9, GAD-7, AUDIT — how they trigger, how to act on positive screens. Email LSW workflow.
Showed how to place medication orders.
Showed how to check pharmacy on Visit tab before signing.
Showed how to send meds to multiple pharmacies simultaneously.
Showed how to confirm med was actually transmitted.
Covered 100-day vs 90-day refill protocol. Medicare meds at 100 days to prevent care gaps.
Saved medication orders with appropriate refill counts and dx attachments.
Placed lab orders as Now vs Future.
LabCorp vs Quest selection (NJ-relevant).
Spotted/resolved red errors before signing.
Medicare hard-stop bypass: Medicare-approved dx list (secure window) OR patient signed waiver (specific pull-down — checking 'patient will sign' alone does NOT work).
Used CAC (calcium-score CT heart) as teaching example since never covered + bypass must be done correctly.
Covered the two pathways: ambulatory order vs telephone encounter.
Ambulatory orders don't show in standard progress-notes view by default. Uncheck 'Hide Additional Visits' to make them visible.
Recommended telephone encounters when documentation matters; brief note explaining patient/staff request.
Critical/abnormal result management: abnormal pap, abnormal mammogram, critical labs. Closed-loop expectations. Reference the patient contract re: results-turnaround time.
Used electronic referrals only. Front office addresses to schedule + track completion.
Confirmed an established referral list is built into provider's Epic orders. If not, alert OM.
Chose the correct SPECIFIC referral (individual provider or office location) — never generic. Generic referrals fall into an unattached basket and never get worked.
Defaulted to Internal referral. Outgoing referral occasionally, only for non-group specialists.
Set up tailored order sets by disease type, age group, visit type (e.g., physical), and other categories. Time investment up front, big payoff.
Note closure timeliness expectations (24–72 hr); consequences of open encounters.
F2 navigation between SmartPhrase fields and asterisk placeholders.
Incident reporting via RLdatix.
Established protected, recurring mentor↔new-hire time on calendar at 30 / 60 / 90 / 180 / 270 days post-start. Email mentor + new hire + pertinent OM(s) to establish.

Reviewed the Meridian Opiates clinical module together. Discussed the practice's approach to continuing care for established opioid patients — the goal is continuity, not reflexive tapering. Provider understands documentation expectations and the PDMP workflow for existing patients.

Reviewed the Meridian Benzos module together. Discussed how to distinguish appropriate continuation of an inherited benzodiazepine prescription from a regimen that warrants a taper conversation — and how to have that conversation without alienating a long-established patient.

Reviewed the Meridian ADHD module together. Discussed stimulant prescribing for established patients, Schedule II documentation requirements, and the practice's expectation that new providers will continue existing regimens for stable patients rather than requiring re-evaluation before every refill.

Six-month controlled substances check-in. Review how the provider has been managing inherited opioid, benzodiazepine, and stimulant patients over the first six months. Are they continuing established care appropriately, or have there been patterns of avoidance, unnecessary tapering, or referral out? Use this as a direct coaching conversation.

Six-month clinical modules check-in. Ask which Meridian modules the provider has used — lipids, CKD, anemia, abdominal pain, ADHD, opiates, benzos. Which have been most useful? Are there modules they have not opened yet that are relevant to their patient population? Identify any clinical areas where they seem to be avoiding complexity and use the modules as a shared reference point for coaching.
